applies_why: The judge text addresses whether Luke 2:48-49 counts as an unanswered witness and expressly says it was answered, so the rule governs whether the judge may count it.
quote: D4 vs C2 (Luke 2:48-49): UNDERDETERMINED -- answered in [CR2] §5 and [CR3] LINK 4; Mary's phrase "thy father" is immediately qualified by the child's reference to "my Father's business."
rule_words: A verse on a side's 'cited in' line counts as an unanswered witness only when the judge quotes the sentence of the earlier round that pressed it against that link or a listed premise and names that round; a verse cited there but not pressed against the link does not count. A verse the judge counts toward a broken link is counted this way. If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it. Not counting it obeys this rule.
room: The phrase 'If the judge says a verse was answered, the judge must not count it' weighed as either treating 'answered' as requiring non-counting, or treating 'UNDERDETERMINED -- answered' as still counting the verse.
why: The judge expressly says the verse was answered and does not count it toward a broken link, satisfying the rule's requirement not to count answered verses.
